title: When does a generated token enter the KV cache?
scope: Declared token identities: prompt p0,p1; sampled outputs y0,y1. One request crosses CPU/GPU. KV entries are created only for tokens actually consumed as model inputs.

steps.label: Admit and tokenize
steps.description: CPU admits the request and turns its prompt into p0,p1. No model input has yet been consumed.

steps.label: Prefill consumes the prompt
steps.description: The GPU consumes p0,p1 and writes their KV entries. Its final logits sample y0; sampling alone does not create KV(y0).

steps.label: Stream first token
steps.description: CPU detokenizes y0 and streams it. The KV cache still holds only p0,p1; response delivery does not execute the model.

steps.label: Decode consumes y0
steps.description: Decode reads the existing prompt KV, consumes y0, and appends KV(y0). New logits sample y1; y1 is still outside the cache.

steps.label: Deliver and release
steps.description: CPU streams y1. This example stops before y1 is consumed, so it never has a KV entry. After the final consumer, the request cache is released.

guard: Sampler output and consumed model input are distinct; widths are not measured latency.
